I would keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the system I know best, it matches the climate and irrigation conditions, and it gives me two harvests from the same land in one year. I would not spread myself across many crops, because I have no formal schooling and I would rather do a simple plan well than chase something riskier. So for this year, I would stay with winter wheat already on the land, then follow it with summer maize after harvest.

For the wheat, I would use improved seed, topdress enough nitrogen to push tillering and grain filling, and give a few irrigations because spring in Hebei can turn dry. I would keep pesticide use moderate, mainly to control aphids, rust, and weeds, because I do not want to spend more than needed. After wheat harvest, I would move straight into hybrid summer maize on the same land. I would use no-tillage for maize to save time and moisture, fertilize more heavily on nitrogen, and irrigate when the crop is establishing and around the key growth stage if rain is short. This is the plan I would trust most because it is familiar, practical, and steady for income and grain output.
